newsitem.title: UK: UK LABOUR ENLISTS SPORTS STARS IN ELECTION DRIVE.
newsitem.headline: UK LABOUR ENLISTS SPORTS STARS IN ELECTION DRIVE.

text.p: The main opposition Labour party paraded a clutch of sporting stars on Thursday in support of its policies to promote sport and put Britain back among the top 10 Olympic nations within a decade.

As in many other areas during Britain's election campaign, Labour promised little in the way of new money. But it pledged to make a difference through better coordination of existing sports bodies and measures to end a decline in school sport.

"I would hope myself that with a coherent commitment based on the approach we've set out... within a decade we can see Britain back where I think it should be -- among the top 10 most successful in the Olympics, for example," Labour's national heritage spokesman, Jack Cunningham, told a news conference.
Among the stars backing Labour were champion javelin thrower Tessa Sanderson, former England rugby union hooker Brian Moore and rugby league scrum half Shaun Edwards.
Sanderson said she would switch to Labour from the Conservatives in next Thursday's election because it was time for a change.

She said she strongly supported Labour's sports policies, especially its promise to stamp out racism in sport. "Racism does not belong in sport and at the end of the day it is sport which flies the flag," she said.

Earlier, businessman Alan Sugar, who has made a fortune as chairman of electronics group Amstrad Plc, said he was switching to Labour because the Conservatives had lost touch with the man in the street.
